question: Q72
title: Fixed native intermediate-state readout connection on complete programs
hypothesis: Can a fixed subtractive native-state connection to the existing output head preserve every originally correct coding and retention case and add coding gains beyond an equal-compute additive connection?
motivation: N56 silent copies preserve all24 native outputs, while both active full and FFN-only copies produce zero valid A/B choices and fail every utility clause. Do not retune their strength/site or send that failed construction into another generation sweep. Test a distinct output connection using only actual same-history native states and a prescribed native-plausibility support. N55 remains engineering-incomplete and censored; no failed cell, reconstruction guard or candidate is recovered.

priors.review_depth: DoLa abstract and method sections2.2/2.3 plus setup3.1 read; alpha0.1 native-probability support and repetition-penalty1.2 are explicit prior settings. Contrastive-reasoning paper abstract only, no full-read claim. No prior coding or Gemma4 benefit assumed.
priors.relation: Known native logit-lens/layer-contrast and contrastive-decoding priors, not a new-method claim or an exact DoLa reproduction. Here subtraction/addition occurs in BF16 hidden readout space before the native head and its softcap, with one fixed architecture boundary. No validation bucket, JSD layer search, learned tuned lens, repetition penalty, fitted direction or strength.

cohort.original_responses_and_grades: 96 exact HOST whole-response carries; original coding55/64 and retention17/32; no original regeneration/rescoring

connection.source_layer: Zero-based native block14 output, computed by num_hidden_layers-num_kv_shared_layers-1: last actual KV-producing block before native shared-KV layers. Fixed by architecture, not ranked or selected from effects.
connection.mature_state: Actual current last-position input to the unchanged native LM head after final native normalization
connection.early_state: Actual same-forward block14 current output, passed through the unchanged native final RMS module directly; no hand-computed reciprocal, fitted lens, bridge or alignment
connection.literal_wiring: z_s=(mature.float()+s*early_normalized.float()).to(native BF16), s=-1 for subtract_native_boundary and +1 for add_native_boundary. Uniform literal coefficients; no optimization or magnitude/energy matching claim. Compute branch using the actual native LM head and exact pinned native final-logit softcap.
connection.scope: A runtime output-head branch/new fixed skip connection using actual native states and pretrained native modules. Base forward, weights, buffers, registered architecture and KV producers remain unchanged. Not full-transformer insertion or serialized expanded-model validation.
connection.native_head_identity_guard: At EVERY actual generated decision, one additional native-head replay from the actual unmodified mature input plus exact native softcap must reproduce actual model logits byte-exact before accepting the new branch. Failure censors the whole panel without changing the guard or replaying completed cells.
connection.support: Use actual native model full-vocabulary FP32 logits on current own history. Eligible iff native_logit >= native_max + log(0.1), inclusive. Alpha0.1 fixed from the DoLa APC prior, not fitted. Native argmax must remain eligible; nonempty support is mandatory. Branch score outside support is -infinity, and next token is full-vocabulary argmax of the explicitly support-constrained branch scores. This is not unrestricted native argmax or an A/B restriction.
connection.filter_identity: Filtering native logits by a support that includes their maximum cannot change native greedy argmax. No filter-only old-response regeneration is performed. This algebraic identity does not imply the branch is useful.
connection.extra_compute: Per fresh decision one actual native final-RMS evaluation on early state and two extra native-head evaluations: unmodified mature replay plus mixed branch. No extra attention/FFN/PLE evaluation, parameter assignment or gradient.
